passage:
A game company released digital pets that lived on phones. Players fed them, played with them, and decorated their rooms.
Some students loved the pets because they were easy to care for. Others said digital pets taught shallow responsibility because real animals need food, space, medical care, and patience.
Their teacher used the debate to discuss simulation and reality.
A digital pet can teach routines and affection, but it cannot fully teach the needs of a living creature. Turning off a phone is not the same as caring for life.
The game was fun. The lesson was that symbols of care are not the same as care itself.
